At first sight, the beach sand appeared "clean," but when we got up close, we found the complete opposite. Most people didn't have to move at all during those 10 minutes. Total tiny pellets: 435 (6.5 grams). Total larger plastic pieces that didn't qualify: 235.5 grams. Total collected from our sample times: 242 grams of plastics. This included 17 bottle caps, 8 straws, 4 strands of fishing wire, and other random plastics. Total non-plastics haul was 278 grams, made of up 27 cigarette buds, random paper, manmade wood, styrofoam, glass, and metals.

The 234 nurdles collected today were exposed by the wind and found in wind-scoured areas on small actively moving dunes created by the strong prevailing north wind. All were found within 50 feet or so of stable vegetated dunes. The fine sand along this section of coast is deposited in the summer and stripped off by winter's storms and currents. The layer where the nurdles were found is about 2 vertical feet below the tops of the current windblown dunes, and could potentially represent the sand level last winter when the nurdles were deposited.
